nesnd_wu_eastern_question_reason: The Toyotomi ended the Warring States with Ming and Wu help, then fought beside the Zheng for Korea. Generations of alliance have tangled the Kyushu garrisons up with the interests of Japan's lords. Now that the South is settled, the court has begun to talk of an eastern expedition: ship the old western army across the sea, raise up the Emperor and the Tokugawa alongside the Toyotomi, give each of the three houses its own lands, and place Kyushu and Shikoku under direct Wu rule. The overseas garrisons and sea trade would all have to be carved up anew.
nesnd_wu_eastern_question_status_offer: The envoys have crossed the sea. No reply has come yet.
nesnd_japan_accept_status_quo_desc: Leave Japan's government and borders as they are. Keep the fleet and the soldiers' pay for the homeland and our other overseas domains.
nesnd_japan_reunification_reason: The alliance across the strait swept away the Toyotomi's rivals, and it also invited the mainland court into Japan's successions, fiefs and wars. Today the taxes of the castle towns flow into many separate treasuries, and every army and merchant answers to a different master. To rebuild a single government, [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] must first bring Honshu together, then take its own affairs, at home and abroad, back into its own hands.
nesnd_japan.1.d: The envoys from Nanjing have brought a plan to partition the realm: Kyoto and Osaka for the Emperor, Edo for the Tokugawa, the rest of Kansai and the Chugoku region for the Toyotomi, and Kyushu and Shikoku under direct Wu rule. The soldiers and taxes of the eastern domains would be split among several houses. The retainers have laid the muster rolls and grain ledgers before [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullName].
nesnd_japan.2.d: Japan's envoys have refused the partition. An expedition means raising money and ships and escorting the three houses into their new domains; the alternative is to withdraw the demand and leave Japan united. The envoys' reply now lies before [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullName].
nesnd_japan.2.d_commander: Japan's envoys have refused the partition. [SCOPE.sCharacter('nesnd_japan_commander').GetFullName] has been ordered to plan the expedition; the officers of the old western army are waiting to sail with him, and the fleet, the pay and the domains' auxiliaries must all come from Nanjing. War, or withdraw the partition?
nesnd_japan.4.d: The fighting over the eastern expedition is done, and Japan has not been divided into three. Fleets and garrisons will redeploy along the current borders, and army funds and trade routes must be handed over item by item. Eastern affairs will be handled under the peace treaties now in force.
nesnd_japan.5.d: At last, all of Honshu answers to one independent government. [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] has taken over the old lords' taxes and armies, and domains that once went their own way now follow a single code of law. The castle-town merchants are waiting for tolls and levies to be settled anew, so they can carry their trade beyond the old domain borders.
nesnd_jp_textiles_reason: Merchants who buy up raw silk and cotton have begun gathering the weavers under one roof. Familiar handwork has moved into bigger mills, where wages come on time and the foreman's rules must be obeyed. People leaving the land have found a new hope; the merchants have tightened their grip on rural production.
nesnd_jp_consumer_goods_reason: The trade in food, furniture and household wares is spreading from a few wealthy houses into many more homes. The men who run these workshops have started to worry about ordinary wages: if customers can barely feed themselves, nothing sells and prices cannot rise.
nesnd_jp_living_standards_reason: Those who have gone into the mills now reckon up the rent, the price of rice and the cost of their children's schooling. The towns owe their labour and their tax revenue to these people, and they want their own share of the prosperity. Whether the government's promise of a new life holds good will be measured by these few expenses.
nesnd_jp_food_supply_reason: The harvest, the fishing boats and the grain dealers feed the towns. When grain prices rise, the grumbling in the markets soon reaches the government offices. Only when carriers are willing to bring food in, and townspeople can afford to buy it, will the streets stay calm.
nesnd_jp_food_processing_reason: The towns need food that keeps and travels, and the grain and fish dealers want buyers outside the harvest season. Canning lets them join buying, processing and shipping into a single business. With food works open, labourers no longer lose their jobs the moment the harvest ends.
nesnd_jp_cohesion_reason: Under the shogunate, the domains, the rural clans and the castle-town merchants each kept order in their own corner. Now schools and government offices tie near and far together, and trade binds more and more livelihoods to one another. Whether life is secure, and whether the country can protect them in war, the people are watching.
nesnd_jp_politics_reason: After unifying Japan, the Toyotomi advanced into Korea with the Wu ruler's aid and secured their domains to the east. The authority of the Ming court, their own armies and Osaka's financial houses sustained the Taiko shogunate. Now new money and new learning have loosened the old hold on power, and merchants, officers and scholars all want a say in state affairs. The quarrels over appointments, the army and the law come down, in the end, to who will run the government.
nesnd_jp_court_reform_reason: The old retainers want reform carried out in the monarch's name. Merchants and officials schooled in the new learning want the law to shield them from arbitrary levies and local strongmen. The crown's name can bring all these people into one room, but each man's rights must still be drawn up, clause by clause.
nesnd_jp_nation_reason: The promises made in the struggle for independence must now be paid out one by one. Who pays for the army, who sets the tariffs, how far local authority reaches: none of it is settled. Those who gave money and those who gave service are all waiting for their place in the new state.
nesnd_jp_new_army_reason: The old armies rested on hereditary warriors and local ties, and every house recruited and drilled in its own way. The country needs organised recruits, trained officers and forces that answer to a single command.
nesnd_jp_open_diplomacy_reason: Tribute and the maritime bans once bound both diplomacy and trade to the overlord's arrangements. Now we must send out merchant ships and open our ports in our own name, and bargain with other countries over our own interests.
nesnd_jp_open_ports_reason: For many years Japan's overseas trade has been penned into a few ports by strict prohibitions. Merchants want raw materials from afar and wider markets for Japanese goods. Those who have lived off the old bans will not give up the ports easily.
nesnd_jp_islands_reason: Honshu is united, but Kyushu and Shikoku have not all been recovered. Their ports and sea lanes are the gateway to southern Japan's trade and defence.
nesnd_jp_choose_court_desc: The dynasty's name can gather old retainers and reformers into one camp. The monarch stays on the throne, new officials are appointed all the same, and both deliberation and enterprise are put to work for the country.\n\nThe policy cannot be changed for #v 12#! months. Changing policy resets reform progress.
nesnd_jp_choose_military_desc: The army needs one command, and orders must be carried through to the end. Let the officers reorganise recruitment and supply, and gather the manpower and money of every province into the nation's defence.\n\nThe policy cannot be changed for #v 12#! months. Changing policy resets reform progress.
nesnd_jp_choose_representative_desc: Those who pay taxes, serve in the ranks and earn a living carry the weight of every state affair. Put more representatives in the chamber, and officials will have to answer in public, and citizens will have a vote to speak with.\n\nThe policy cannot be changed for #v 12#! months. Changing policy resets reform progress.
nesnd_jp_development.1.d: Foreign envoys now come straight to our government. The defence and overseas affairs we once handled through an overlord now run on rules of our own.\n\nThe merchants and local men who backed independence have not gone home. They are at our door with new petitions, asking the government to keep its old promises.
nesnd_jp_development.2.d: The new rules for appointing officials have taken hold, and the laws have redrawn how much power each class holds. Those who once ran their districts by right of birth must now work within posts and powers set by the government. The officials, soldiers and merchants who carried the reform are finding their places in the new order.
nesnd_jp_foreign_reason: Troops from the mainland court helped the Toyotomi subdue Japan, and ever since, tribute and sea trade have been tangled up with the politics of the islands. Every measure of autonomy we win costs the overlord a measure of revenue, naval security and control over Japan. Those interests will not vanish just because the old treaty is dissolved.
nesnd_jp_seek_capital_cne_desc: Use the promise of commercial cooperation as our opening, and ask the northern government to fund factories in Japan.\n\nAfter receiving assistance, further funding is unavailable for #v 3#! years.
nesnd_jp_seek_capital_hus_desc: On the strength of trade and industry, ask Dongzhou for money to build workshops.\n\nAfter receiving assistance, further funding is unavailable for #v 3#! years.
nesnd_jp_seek_capital_usm_desc: The southern government has traded with Japan for many years. Follow those old connections and ask for a grant: capital for our workshops, and craftsmen to train our own.\n\nAfter receiving assistance, further funding is unavailable for #v 3#! years.
nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d1: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] wants a larger hand in its own affairs and asks us to loosen the terms of its subordination. Its envoy says that with more autonomy they would not need to wait on our approval for every domestic matter, while the ties between our countries would stay as they are.
nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d2: An envoy from [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] demands an end to the subject relationship. From now on they would run their own diplomacy, army and trade, and deal with us as an independent country.
nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d4: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] is raising money to build workshops. Its envoy asks us for a grant to help expand production and train skilled workers.
nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d5: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] proposes a settlement over southern Korea. Its government offers to relinquish claims to Busan and Yangho and transfer any territory it still holds there to Korea. The envoy asks us to close this old case for good.
nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d7: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] seeks our permission to negotiate union with other Japanese subjects. Its government would lead the union, with each invited country surrendering its separate government only by consent.
nesnd_jp_foreign.2.d: Our envoy has brought word from [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_partner').GetNameNoFormatting]: they have agreed.
nesnd_jp_foreign.3.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_partner').GetNameNoFormatting] has turned down the terms our envoy carried. They would not give an inch, and relations between our countries are the worse for it.
nesnd_jp_development.2.d_court: A new law has fixed the rules for deliberation and appointment. The old retainers still stand beside the monarch, but a different kind of official, versed in practical affairs, has begun to fill the provincial offices.\n\nReformers loyal to the dynasty believe these concessions will let the monarchy endure. Whether those who have won a voice will rest content with it, no one can say.
nesnd_jp_development.2.d_representative: Those entitled to vote now choose their representatives, and newspapers can debate the conduct of government. Officials face new rules of appointment, while political argument has spread beyond the old ruling families.\n\nThe new schools keep bringing more people into this world.
nesnd_jp_establish_edo_reason: Edo now rules wide lands in the north. Its garrisons can hold the roads, but they cannot run the provinces. The government must hire officials and bring revenue and spending into a single ledger, and the castle towns must make room for merchants, craftsmen and people come from afar to find work. Only when these places can carry the daily business of government will Edo have its hands free to seek greater powers.
nesnd_jp_establish_kyoto_reason: The courtiers of Kyoto and the merchants of Osaka each have their own circles and their own calculations. Court titles do not pay soldiers, and merchants' money does not flow into the treasury of its own accord. The officials in charge of revenue must put the income and business of the present territories in order, so that the two cities can support the new government.
nesnd_jp_establish_toyotomi_reason: Since the partition, the Toyotomi can no longer command all of Japan. Yet not one of the soldiers and retainers in the western provinces has gone, and all of them wait for their rice stipends. Old prestige alone can no longer decide where the annual tax is collected or who governs the villages. The Toyotomi regime must set up reliable magistrates' offices in the lands it still holds, and make the castle towns into places for collecting taxes, doing government business and hiring labour.
nesnd_jp_foreign.2.d1: Our overlord has agreed to loosen its hold, raising us one step towards autonomy. The two governments have agreed a five-year truce. Matters that once needed permission at every turn can now be taken in hand ourselves.
nesnd_jp_foreign.2.d4: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_partner').GetNameNoFormatting] has agreed to provide development funds, so the money to expand workshops and train craftsmen has been found. No further grant of this kind will be available for three years.
nesnd_jp_foreign.2.d5: The Korean settlement has been accepted. Our claims to Busan and Yangho have been withdrawn, and any territory we still held there has passed to Korea.
